chunks: He [al-Mufid] said: Abu Ubaydillah Muhammad ibn Imran al-Marzbani informed me, saying: Muhammad ibn Ahmad al-Hakimi narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Ishaq narrated to us, saying: Yahya ibn Ma'in informed us, saying: Abd al-Razzaq narrated to us, saying: Ma'mar informed us, from Thabit, from Anas ibn Malik, who said: The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and his family and grant them peace, said:
"Whenever vulgarity is present in anything, it only tarnishes it; and whenever modesty is present in anything, it only adorns it."
ai.seo_question: What did the Prophet Muhammad say about vulgarity and modesty?
ai.summary: This prophetic tradition, transmitted through a Basran chain via the prominent companion Anas ibn Malik, presents a concise maxim contrasting two moral qualities. The Prophet declares that vulgarity (fuhsh) invariably degrades whatever it touches, while modesty (haya') invariably beautifies it. The hadith was likely addressed to a general audience as moral instruction, using the rhetorical device of parallel antithesis to make the teaching memorable. In early Islamic society, haya' encompassed both inner bashfulness before God and outward decorum in speech and conduct.

en.mulla-asgharali-m-m-jaffer: 2. He said: Abu Abdillah Muhammad ibn Imran al-Marzbani reported to me from Muhammad ibn Ahmad al-Hakimi, who reported from Muhammad ibn Ishaq, who reported from Yahya ibn Moeen, who reported from Abdul Razzaq, who reported from Mo’mar, from Thabit, from Anas ibn Malik that: The Prophet, peace be upon him and his progeny, said:
"Whenever there is any vulgarity in any affair, it does not leave it without being tarnished; and whenever there is bashfulness in any matter, it does not leave it without being adorned."
